definition: The Ruzzo–Tompa algorithm or the RT algorithm is a linear-time algorithm for finding all non-overlapping, contiguous, maximal scoring subsequences in a sequence of real numbers.
details: The Ruzzo–Tompa algorithm was proposed by Walter L. Ruzzo and Martin Tompa. This algorithm is an improvement over previously known quadratic time algorithms. The maximum scoring subsequence from the set produced by the algorithm is also a solution to the maximum subarray problem. The Ruzzo–Tompa algorithm has applications in bioinformatics, web scraping, and information retrieval.

explainer.lead: The Ruzzo–Tompa algorithm finds all non-overlapping, contiguous, maximal scoring subsequences in a sequence of real numbers in linear time. It matters as an improvement over previously known quadratic time algorithms for this task.

tiers.eli5: It picks out the best-scoring stretches in a long list of numbers without comparing every possible pair of stretches.
tiers.practitioner: Used for scoring-subsequence search in sequence data; a pitfall is that the result set is non-overlapping, so it is not a list of all high-scoring windows.
tiers.paperLevel: A linear-time algorithm, proposed by Walter L. Ruzzo and Martin Tompa, that returns all non-overlapping, contiguous, maximal scoring subsequences; the maximum scoring subsequence from the set also solves the maximum subarray problem. Limits: linear-time improvement over quadratic approaches; outputs non-overlapping subsequences only.

explainer.example: Given a sequence of real numbers, the algorithm returns the set of non-overlapping maximal scoring subsequences, and the highest-scoring one among them is a maximum subarray.
